data.title: A recent study suggests that insects branched out from crustaceans
data.author: Carrok
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一种在凯科斯群岛发现的 remipede 物种，这是一种与昆虫有密切亲缘关系的甲壳类动物。通过系统发生学的研究，科学家发现昆虫实际上属于广义的甲壳类动物群，特别是与虾和蟹等同属 pancrustacea 组。2023年的一项研究进一步确认昆虫与名为 remipede 的甲壳类动物是近亲，尽管两者外观差异很大。这种系统分类变化不仅重新排列了生物进化树，还帮助科学家更好地理解生命复杂性及物种多样化模式。文章还通过鸟类与恐龙、鲸鱼与有蹄类哺乳动物的例子，说明这类系统发生学发现对理解进化史和生物适应性的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：昆虫与甲壳类动物的进化关系及其引发的讨论

不同观点：
• [adrian_b] 认为文章标题应提及2023年以体现“近期”研究。他指出昆虫从水蚤类甲壳动物演化而来的观点已有十多年历史，2023年的研究只是提供了更强证据。他还强调，多足类动物（如马陆和蜈蚣）与昆虫的关系比之前认为的更远，且多足类更早独立适应陆地生活。
• [Imnimo] 对进化的传统“海洋生物爬上岸”的简化模型提出质疑，询问是否存在从陆地返回海洋的演化例子。
• [nmstoker] 指出文章中对“虫子”一词的使用不符合技术定义，并提供了相关维基百科链接以供参考。

补充讨论：
• [abeindoria] 推荐了Neil Shubin的《Your Inner Fish》一书，建议对进化话题感兴趣的人阅读。
• [ljsprague] 提供了一个关于树栖虾的链接，作为对[Imnimo]关于陆地到海洋演化问题的回应。
• [willis936] 猜测甲壳类过敏实际上可能是节肢动物过敏，但承认缺乏相关研究支持。
• [dboreham] 认为沿海洞穴是生物从水生到陆生实验的理想环境，并批评一些科学家在没有事实基础的情况下做出结论。
• [upghost] 引用xkcd漫画，以幽默方式质疑“万物演化成螃蟹”的观点。
• [anigbrowl] 和 [fallat] 都表示对讨论内容感到惊讶或觉得显而易见。
• [epicureanideal] 质疑这是否是“食用昆虫”宣传的一部分，并表达了对甲壳类食物的反感。

争议焦点：
• 对“虫子”一词的技术性使用存在争议（[nmstoker]）。
• 对科学文章中演化结论的可靠性和科学家的研究方法存在质疑（[dboreham]）。
• 对是否存在从陆地返回海洋的演化例子进行探讨（[Imnimo], [ljsprague]）。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 对甲壳类过敏本质的新猜测（[willis936]）。
• 对进化论中幽默元素的引用（[upghost]）。
• 对文章潜在商业动机（“食用昆虫”宣传）的怀疑（[epicureanideal]）。

43658093.article_content:
A species of remipede known from the Caicos Islands. The photograph was taken by a member of a
multinational team
looking for rare species. Remipedes are crustaceans that are close relatives to insects.
Jørgen Olesen / Natural History Museum of Denmark, Brett Gonzalez, Karen Osborn, GGI
Shrimp look an awful lot like bugs. The exoskeletons, jointed legs and compound eyes of both groups of living things give them more than a passing resemblance to each other, so no wonder some people call shrimp-like crawfish “
mudbugs
,” and a tattoo reading “
shrimps is bugs
” became a viral meme for underscoring the resemblance. But the tattoo got the reality backwards. Shrimp are not bugs. Bugs—or, more properly, insects—are technically a form of crustacean.
Biologists of many different subdisciplines categorize life in a field called systematics. Living things of all sorts, both extant and extinct, are constantly being compared and evaluated to build what we so commonly think of as the tree of life. The addition of new species and novel analyses are constantly reshaping that evolutionary tree, and sometimes the category changes shift more than just a few twigs but entire evolutionary branches. Birds are now known to be dinosaurs, for example, whales are technically hoofed mammals called artiodactyls, and, thanks to
a 2023 study
in
Molecular Biology and Evolution
, insects have been shifted into the same group as shrimp and crabs called pancrustacea.
The realization that bugs were close relatives of crustaceans took almost a century of curiosity to uncover. Paleontologist Joanna Wolfe of Harvard University, one of the authors of the 2023 study, notes that researchers noticed some insects and crustaceans had the same structures in their eyes and nervous systems. The resemblance could have been the result of convergent evolution, when two groups independently evolve in the same way, and so the idea that insects are modified crustaceans didn’t catch. But the hypothesis didn’t fully go away, either.
In 2013, Wolfe and colleagues found that insects were the sister group, or next closest evolutionary relatives, to crustaceans called remipedes—which live in undersea caves and are the only venomous crustaceans. Remipedes were supposed to be oddballs that were shaped in strange ways due to their lives in caves. Now they were coming out as the closest relatives to the flies, mantises, bees and other insects we see around us on land. “At that time, I was shocked and thought there was something wrong with our results,” Wolfe recalls, only to have additional evidence make the connection between insects and crustaceans stronger. The 2023 analysis, based on genetic data, found insects next to remipedes in the middle of the various crustacean subgroups. Specifically, insects fit within a wide group of crustaceans called
allotriocarida
that not only includes remipedes, but also other unusual groups such as shrimp-like branchiopods and worm-like cephalocarids sometimes called “horseshoe shrimp.” To put it another way, insects are to crustaceans as bats are to mammals—a subset that belongs to a broader group despite seeming so different from their closest relatives.
Systematic shifts do far more than simply rearrange who’s related to whom. “Systematics allow us to make sense of the complexity of life,” says Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History paleontologist Advait Jukar. “When we recategorize species into new groups we can look at patterns of how that group might be diversifying and the various environmental and ecological factors.”
Insects, like those above, fit right in the middle of the broader crustacean family tree.
Richard Ross, The Image Bank via Getty Images
When birds were recognized as dinosaurs, the change did more than reshuffle their place on the evolutionary tree. “The change showed us how characteristics that we typically associate with birds today, such as feathers, hollow bones and air sacs, were widely found within Dinosauria,” Jukar says. Paleontologists began finding more feathered dinosaurs and dinosaurs with traits previously associated with birds, such as complex systems of air sacs as part of their respiratory systems, once the connection was made. The newly understood relationship between birds and other dinosaurs has allowed experts to better understand
why only birds survived
the mass extinction of 66 million years ago. Comparisons between birds and bird-like dinosaurs revealed that adaptations for eating seeds and nuts that some birds developed during the Cretaceous allowed them to survive while bird-like raptors perished.
The recognition that whales are hoofed mammals occurred around the same time as birds were found to be dinosaurs. The shift had a deep effect on how paleontologists carried out their research as well as the identity of the blubbery mammals. Prior to the 1990s, the earliest whales were thought to have evolved from carnivorous mammals called mesonychids. The beasts, sometimes called “w

data.title: You might not need WebSockets
data.author: hntrl
data.article_summary: WebSocket是一种允许客户端与服务器之间建立双向通信的协议，适用于实时应用。然而，WebSocket消息不具备事务性，无法确保消息的顺序和处理状态，这可能导致在处理状态对象或需要确认的消息时出现复杂性。例如，当操作导致错误时，由于消息流无法直接关联，错误处理变得困难。此外，WebSocket需要管理连接的生命周期，包括处理连接的打开、关闭和错误事件。对于需要确认的操作，使用HTTP等更具事务性的协议可能更为合适。WebSocket适合处理无需确认的消息，如心跳或键盘输入。因此，在某些情况下，可能并不需要WebSocket。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebSocket、HTTP2、SSE（Server-Sent Events）、长轮询（Long Polling）等通信技术在不同场景下的优缺点及适用性

不同观点：
• [hombre_fatal] 认为在严肃的应用中使用 `send(message).then(res => ...)` 这种带有请求/响应周期的API是值得的，虽然WebSocket与HTTP服务器的整合确实有些混乱，但这些特性是可以习惯和适应的。相比EventSource，WebSocket的浏览器API更易用。
• [osigurdson] 反驳了关于视频流通过WebSocket实现的观点，指出视频流通常是通过范围请求（range requests）分块加载的，而不是通过单一的长连接实现的。
• [socketcluster] 认为HTTP2的服务器推送功能是后来添加的，增加了不必要的开销和安全挑战。WebSocket则是为双向通信设计的更简单的协议，提供了对数据流和连接状态的更好控制，并且在处理认证和访问控制时更为简便。
• [notpushkin] 提出可以使用SSE（Server-Sent Events）作为替代方案，认为它是一个更简单的选择。
• [toomim] 推荐了Braid-HTTP协议，认为它通过扩展HTTP事件流，能够提供一个健壮的状态同步协议。
• [collingreen] 表达了对在项目中使用WebSocket后看到相关讨论的感慨，暗示了对WebSocket复杂性的担忧。
• [djfobbz] 分享了其使用WebSocket构建工业级监控应用的经验，认为WebSocket是非常稳定且易于维护的，质疑文章中将WebSocket复杂化的倾向。
• [efortis] 提供了长轮询的实现示例，展示了在没有WebSocket的情况下如何通过长轮询实现类似的实时功能。
• [oneoverten] 质疑WebSocket的必要性，认为即使使用流式传输，仍然需要处理连接管理和同步问题。
• [wewewedxfgdf] 分享了自己的经验，放弃了WebSocket而选择HTTP长轮询和POST请求，认为这更简单。
• [sneilan1] 建议使用AWS AppSync事件服务而不是自己实现WebSocket服务器，质疑自己构建服务器的必要性。
• [givemeethekeys] 认为复杂性可以通过使用框架来解决，框架可以让WebSocket像REST一样易用。
• [bmitc] 将WebSocket视为一种增强版的TCP，用于实现消息功能，而不是HTTP的替代品。
• [almosthere] 欣赏vert.x的策略，能够根据可用性无缝降级连接形式，提供灵活性。
• [RajT88] 支持简化技术选择，认为很多技术潮流（如Kubernetes、云、复杂数据库）增加了不必要的复杂性，支持更简单的解决方案。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点：WebSocket的复杂性和适用场景。部分开发者认为WebSocket提供了更好的控制和性能，而另一些开发者则认为HTTP2、SSE、长轮询等技术更简单且足够用。
- 其他技术如SSE、长轮询和框架的使用被认为是简化WebSocket复杂性的替代方案或解决方案。
- 强调了技术选择的复杂性和不必要复杂性的风险，支持更简单和适合具体场景的技术方案。

43659370.article_content:
Whatâs a WebSocket?
If youâre new to web development or you havenât heard of a WebSocket before, theyâre a way to open a two-way communication channel between the client and server using HTTP as the transport protocol. In less nerdy terms, itâs a way to keep an open line of communication between the client and server so that both can send and receive messages at any time. (
MDN Reference
)
Because of how itâs advertised on the tin, itâs natural to think of a WebSocket as the best (and sometimes only) way to orchestrate a long-living stream of data between client and server, like for instance a real time application. In practice though, it turns out there are a few reasons why you might not want to use them:
WebSocket messages arenât transactional
I see a lot of instances where WebSockets are used as the way of maintaining consistency for some kind of state object. For instance, you use the transmitting side of the socket to represent mutations to some object, and the receiving side of the socket to represent state as it gets changed by those mutations. That way if you have multiple clients listening to the same object, theyâll all see the same state changes without having to refresh the page.
# Client 1
>>> { command: "increment", amount: 5 }
<<< { event: "count", value: 5 }
>>> { command: "decrement", amount: 2 }
<<< { event: "count", value: 3 }
# Client 2
<<< { event: "count", value: 5 }
<<< { event: "count", value: 3 }
But what if you placed some kind of invariant condition on the state object? For instance, you want to make sure that the count is never negative:
<<< { event: "count", amount: 5 }
>>> { command: "decrement", amount: 6 }
<<< { error: "count cannot be negative" }
The issue here is that thereâs no association between the mutation and error message since the error message will be received on the same stream as every other message. We canât reliably say âthe next messageâ received on the stream is the result of the previous command since the server could have sent any number of messages in between now and then.
If we wanted to update the UI to show the error, weâd have to link the error event somehow (like providing an associative request id in the command and the error message):
>>> { command: "decrement", amount: 6, requestId: "123" }
<<< { error: "count cannot be negative", requestId: "123" }
This becomes even more awkward because now you have to keep track of every message you send, and you have to find some way to bubble the error event back to the UI in an idempotent way. The same goes if you wanted to have some kind of indication that the command was received by the server. In that case, now youâre also dealing with certain hard-to-track edge cases:
What if the socket closes before the server can process the command?
What if you never receive a response message on the socket for some reason?
What if youâre dealing with a huge number of concurrent requests?
It creates too many unknowns and complexity for something that should be simple. If youâre dealing with messages where you need to know if they were received or not, youâre better off with using a more transactional protocol like HTTP to represent the sending side of the socket.
( < > ) = HTTP
( <<< >>> ) = WebSocket
# Success
> POST /increment '{ value: 5 }'
< 200 OK
<<< { event: "count", value: 5 }
#- (the update message still gets sent to all connected clients)
# Failure
> POST /decrement '{ value: 6 }'
< 400 Bad Request
#- (no update gets sent because the request failed)
Weâve effectively ditched the transmitting side of the socket altogether and replaced it with HTTP, which means weâre now leaning on WebSockets to represent only one stream of data (the receiving side). As it turns out thereâs other ways to do that donât require the overhead of a full duplex connection.
(weâll get into this later)
If youâre sending messages that donât necessarily need to be acknowledged (like a heartbeat or keyboard inputs), then Websockets make a great fit. Hence the title of this post, you
might
not need Websockets.
You have to manage the socket lifecycle
When you use WebSockets, youâre not just sending and receiving messages at willâyour application also has to respond to the opening and closing of the connection. This means handling events like âopenâ and âcloseâ (or âerrorâ), deciding what to do during reconnect attempts, and cleaning up resources when the connection is no longer needed.

43659370.article_summary: WebSocket是一种允许客户端与服务器之间建立双向通信的协议，适用于实时应用。然而，WebSocket消息不具备事务性，无法确保消息的顺序和处理状态，这可能导致在处理状态对象或需要确认的消息时出现复杂性。例如，当操作导致错误时，由于消息流无法直接关联，错误处理变得困难。此外，WebSocket需要管理连接的生命周期，包括处理连接的打开、关闭和错误事件。对于需要确认的操作，使用HTTP等更具事务性的协议可能更为合适。WebSocket适合处理无需确认的消息，如心跳或键盘输入。因此，在某些情况下，可能并不需要WebSocket。

• [hombre_fatal] 认为在严肃的应用中使用 `send(message).then(res => ...)` 这种带有请求/响应周期的API是值得的，虽然WebSocket与HTTP服务器的整合确实有些混乱，但这些特性是可以习惯和适应的。相比EventSource，WebSocket的浏览器API更易用。
• [osigurdson] 反驳了关于视频流通过WebSocket实现的观点，指出视频流通常是通过范围请求（range requests）分块加载的，而不是通过单一的长连接实现的。
• [socketcluster] 认为HTTP2的服务器推送功能是后来添加的，增加了不必要的开销和安全挑战。WebSocket则是为双向通信设计的更简单的协议，提供了对数据流和连接状态的更好控制，并且在处理认证和访问控制时更为简便。

• [wewewedxfgdf] 分享了自己的经验，放弃了WebSocket而选择HTTP长轮询和POST请求，认为这更简单。
• [sneilan1] 建议使用AWS AppSync事件服务而不是自己实现WebSocket服务器，质疑自己构建服务器的必要性。
• [givemeethekeys] 认为复杂性可以通过使用框架来解决，框架可以让WebSocket像REST一样易用。

• [RajT88] 支持简化技术选择，认为很多技术潮流（如Kubernetes、云、复杂数据库）增加了不必要的复杂性，支持更简单的解决方案。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点：WebSocket的复杂性和适用场景。部分开发者认为WebSocket提供了更好的控制和性能，而另一些开发者则认为HTTP2、SSE、长轮询等技术更简单且足够用。
- 其他技术如SSE、长轮询和框架的使用被认为是简化WebSocket复杂性的替代方案或解决方案。
- 强调了技术选择的复杂性和不必要复杂性的风险，支持更简单和适合具体场景的技术方案。

data.title: Vacheron Constantin breaks the world record for most complicated wristwatch
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: Vacheron Constantin的Les Cabinotiers部门推出了世上最复杂的腕表——“Solaria Ultra Grand Complication”，拥有41种复杂功能和13项潜在专利，设计现代且尺寸适于佩戴。该表拥有1521个组件和204颗宝石，功能包括天文和报时复杂装置，以及独立运作的格列高利万年历和第二时区显示。与之前的“Berkley Grand Complication”大口袋表不同，Solaria是完全由Vacheron主导的项目，历时八年制作，仅由一位制表师完成，且无固定价格，但接受定制订单，每块表都独一无二。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机械表（尤其是高端瑞士机械表）的功能、价值、术语、经济模式以及与现代智能手表的对比。

不同观点：
• **赞赏机械表的技术与工艺**：一些评论（如light_triad和mofunnyman）对机械表的复杂结构和精湛工艺表示赞赏，认为其设计和功能非常了不起，甚至用"fuckin nuts"来形容其精妙。
• **对高端机械表场景的反感**：pixelpoet对高端机械表的术语和文化表示反感，认为其术语过于 pompous（ pompous terminology），并且不喜欢与该领域相关的人。
• **享受奢侈品的乐趣**：rpicard指出，无论支持还是反对奢侈手表，人们喜欢它们是因为这很有趣（"it’s fun"），并推荐了一期关于劳力士的播客。
• **质疑经济模式**：atonse和litoE对高端机械表的经济可行性表示疑问，质疑这些高价低产量的产品是否有足够的市场需求。atonse特别提到了Vacheron Constantin和Richard Mille等品牌如何盈利。

补充讨论：
• **对复杂功能的调侃**：bradfitz和nradov以幽默的方式质疑机械表的复杂功能是否值得骄傲，nradov特别提到没有GPS功能，无法与现代技术（如Strava）兼容。
• **品牌与识别**：paulsutter提到购买奢侈手表的社交功能，即通过手表识别身份，但最终大多数人还是选择佩戴Apple Watch。他还批评了Apple Watch的软件体验。
• **对手表字体和设计的批评**：dole对Vacheron Constantin的logo字体表示不满，认为其设计显得廉价且刺眼，尽管整体设计和技术都很优秀。
• **价格与社会地位的隐喻**：jsheard用一句常见的奢侈品市场说法（"if you have to ask..."）来暗示手表的高价，而iFire则以幽默的方式将现代智能手机与传统机械表进行对比。
• **历史记录的提及**：michaelssilver提到了Patek Philippe曾保持的复杂功能记录，补充了关于奢侈手表品牌竞争的历史背景。

争议焦点：
• **机械表的复杂性是否值得骄傲**：部分评论（如bradfitz和nradov）质疑机械表的复杂功能是否实际，并将其与现代技术（如GPS和智能手表）进行对比。
• **奢侈手表的文化与经济可行性**：一些评论（如atonse和litoE）质疑高端机械表的市场需求和经济模式，而另一些评论（如rpicard）则强调了享受奢侈品的乐趣和社交功能。

总的来说，讨论围绕机械表的工艺、文化、经济模式及其与现代技术的比较展开，参与者从不同角度表达了对奢侈手表的赞赏、质疑和幽默看法。

Vacheron Constantin's Les Cabinotiers department has done it again, setting a world record for the most complicated wristwatch with the "Solaria Ultra Grand Complication" less than one year after
the announcement of the world's most complicated watch
. Far from a pocket watch this time, the Solaria features 41 complications, 13 potential patented inventions, and a shockingly modern design and wearable size. Fair warning, this story will (yet again) be the longest we'll run during Watches and Wonders.
Obviously, the brand is no stranger to high-complication watchmaking over their 270-year history. Their forays into this mini-competition among the world's complications specialists resulted in 2017's Vacheron Constantin Les Cabinotiers Celestia Astronomical Grand Complication 3600, with 23 complications. But they still didn't have nearly the number of complications of the Franck Muller Aeternitas Mega 4, with its 36. But Franck Muller's website is wildly out of date. Not only has the Aeternitas not been the most complicated
watch
for some time, but it's no longer the most complicated wristwatch either.
Video: Unraveling The Story Of The Vacheron Constantin Berkley Grand Complication
Less than a year ago, Vacheron Constantin made the most complicated watch in the world and we were there
to bring you a video about the watch.
Beyond the awe at the Berkley Grand Comp, there was some fair critique that the 960 gram, 90.8mm diameter by 50.55mm thick "pocket watch" wasn't so much a watch, but a clock (though, where the line of one ends and the other begins is up for debate) or – my favorite comment – a horological kettlebell. "Impressive. Now make a wristwatch version," said one reader. Well, they kind of just did.
As they did last year for that watch, Vacheron yet again previewed the Les Cabinotiers Solari this year on the day before Watches and Wonders to a select group of press. That means that, not only do we have all the details, but I also had a chance to go "hands-on” (literally, versus the Berkley which we couldn’t touch) with the watch.
Overview
Alright, we know that the watch has 41 complications and has 13 patents applied for – and we'll get to the specific complications shortly – but I think one of the most impressive things is the size and overall aesthetic of the watch. Vacheron has not shied from tying the idea of "complicated" closely to the word "loud" with watches like the
2022 Tribute to Bacchus
, and yet, this has a relatively reserved case design and modern dial language in a wearable package.
How wearable? The watch measures 45mm by 14.99mm thick. Compare that to the recent Omega Seamaster Planet Ocean World Time, which is 0.5mm larger and 4mm
thicker
. While these are two different watches with two different use cases (the "Solaria" has no listed water resistance, so I'd say it's just dust-proof), and Vacheron's offering is a unique piece from their high watchmaking arm with no price given, it just goes to show the achievement of micro-mechanics and miniaturisation from Vacheron.
The entire movement, the Calibre 3655, measures only 36mm in diameter by 10.96mm thick and features everything from 14 astronomical complications to five chiming complications, including a split-second chronograph that also doubles as one of those astronomical complications, and more. With 1521 components and 204 jewels, the watch runs at 3Hz with a 72-hour power reserve.
Unlike the Berkley Grand Complication, which was made on commission, the Solaria is a fully Vacheron-driven project. One watchmaker, yes, just one, was given
carte blanche
to go hog wild and make the most incredible feat of horology he could, and spent eight years on the task. He certainly took full advantage of the brief. There was no budget, and there is no price tag but the watch is for sale. In fact, the Solaria is actually called “the Premiere” to end its official name, because the program is open to orders with future examples modified in ways to keep them all unique. Yet each would have the full suite of complications. We will have a list of all the complications at the end, but here are some highlights.
Yes, there are the normal (and extremely complex) chiming complications, a chronograph, and a tourbillon, but in this case, the Westminster minute repeater mechanism is integrated into the base movement along with the chronograph mechanism and tourbillon regulator. The Civil time display module is also coupled to the base movement, while Sidereal time runs independently.
There is a Gregorian perpetual calendar and a second time zone display. But the second time zone has an independent hour and minute hands for your local time that are separated from the home time, and another worldtime display. The as

data.title: AI Coding and the Peanut Butter and Jelly Problem
data.author: tylerg
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在理解和执行指令方面的能力，尤其是在编程、图像/视频处理等领域的应用和挑战，以及如何优化与LLM的沟通方式。

不同观点：
• **kenjackson** 认为LLM在理解文本指令方面表现优异，甚至优于人类，但在图像和视频生成方面远不如人类。他通过“项目管理秋千”故事类比说明问题，指出LLM在不同任务上的表现差异。

• **iDon** 强调了高层次语言和规范语言的长期梦想，认为我们正在进入一个新的阶段。他提到在提示（prompt）中清晰定义术语的重要性，并预测提示语言将进一步演变，类似于MCP成为连接LLM与其他应用的标准API。他还指出，过去的规范语言往往严格，因为其目的是生成可证明正确的代码，而提示语言可以更灵活地应用。

• **zahlman** 质疑如果一个人已经有能力清晰地沟通和定义需求，为何还需要AI来写代码。他认为，如果代码编写不简单，那么问题可能出在工具或架构上，而不是AI的价值。

• **Syzygies** 通过比喻说明AI工具的使用需要技巧和经验。他认为，虽然AI能极大地提高效率，但并不是每个人都能轻易学会如何最大化其潜力。他分享了自己在数学研究中使用AI编码的经验，认为理解代码仍是必要的。

• **daxfohl** 建议使用类似BASIC的协议来指导LLM，认为这样可以避免混淆英语和结构化编程概念，并且可以更灵活地调整和插入步骤，从而提高沟通的精确性。

补充讨论：
• **Peanut Butter and Jelly（花生酱和果冻）问题** 被多次提及，作为一个经典的指令执行和需求分析的教学例子。这个例子展示了清晰沟通和精确指令的重要性，并引发了关于如何有效与AI沟通的讨论。

• **争议焦点** 在于LLM在不同任务上的有效性和实际应用中的沟通挑战。部分评论者认为AI的价值在于其能够简化编码过程，而另一些人则质疑其必要性，尤其对于已经能清晰表达需求的人。

• **历史背景和教育** 提及花生酱和果冻问题在不同教育阶段的应用，显示了这一问题在计算机科学教育中的普遍性和持久性。

• **工具和语言演变** 一些评论者讨论了提示语言的演变和标准化需求，以及从历史编程语言（如BASIC）中汲取灵感来优化与LLM的交互方式。

• **iDon** 强调了高层次语言和规范语言的长期梦想，认为我们正在进入一个新的阶段。他提到在提示（prompt）中清晰定义术语的重要性，并预测提示语言将进一步演变，类似于MCP成为连接LLM与其他应用的标准API。他还指出，过去的规范语言往往严格，因为其目的是生成可证明正确的代码，而提示语言可以更灵活地应用。

• **zahlman** 质疑如果一个人已经有能力清晰地沟通和定义需求，为何还需要AI来写代码。他认为，如果代码编写不简单，那么问题可能出在工具或架构上，而不是AI的价值。

• **Syzygies** 通过比喻说明AI工具的使用需要技巧和经验。他认为，虽然AI能极大地提高效率，但并不是每个人都能轻易学会如何最大化其潜力。他分享了自己在数学研究中使用AI编码的经验，认为理解代码仍是必要的。

• **daxfohl** 建议使用类似BASIC的协议来指导LLM，认为这样可以避免混淆英语和结构化编程概念，并且可以更灵活地调整和插入步骤，从而提高沟通的精确性。

补充讨论：
• **Peanut Butter and Jelly（花生酱和果冻）问题** 被多次提及，作为一个经典的指令执行和需求分析的教学例子。这个例子展示了清晰沟通和精确指令的重要性，并引发了关于如何有效与AI沟通的讨论。

• **争议焦点** 在于LLM在不同任务上的有效性和实际应用中的沟通挑战。部分评论者认为AI的价值在于其能够简化编码过程，而另一些人则质疑其必要性，尤其对于已经能清晰表达需求的人。

• **历史背景和教育** 提及花生酱和果冻问题在不同教育阶段的应用，显示了这一问题在计算机科学教育中的普遍性和持久性。

• **工具和语言演变** 一些评论者讨论了提示语言的演变和标准化需求，以及从历史编程语言（如BASIC）中汲取灵感来优化与LLM的交互方式。

data.article_summary:
文章总结了欧盟消费者保护合作网络发布的关于游戏内虚拟货币的指导原则。该文件为解释现行的欧盟消费者保护法提供了建议，并非具有法律效力。各国有权自行决定是否采纳这些建议。主要原则包括：

1. 游戏内货币若主要用于购买游戏内物品，则被视为真实货币的数字代表。
2. 游戏内交易在消费者权益保护方面等同于真实世界交易。
3. 禁止利用认知偏见诱导玩家多付费或少获利。
4. 必须同时显示游戏币和真实货币的价格。
5. 建议不引入多种货币和复杂的兑换链。
6. 建议不强迫玩家购买超出需求的货币。
7. 交易须附带详细信息，玩家有权在14天内取消交易。
8. 若产品与描述不符，玩家可取消交易。
9. 推荐部分交易回滚，退还剩余未使用货币的真实资金。
10. 游戏运营商应避免复杂条款，小心处理易受伤害的玩家，如儿童或有赌博成瘾问题的玩家。
11. 应实施家长控制功能。

遵循这些建议对开发者来说可能复杂且昂贵，尤其是对中小型企业。同时，若仅针对欧盟市场，可能影响全球发行策略。

43658420.article_content:
Key principles on in-game virtual currencies in the EU
en
ru
Last month, the
Consumer Protection Cooperation Network
, in coordination with the European Commission, released interesting guidelines on the implementation of in-game currencies.
News
The document
on my Google Drive — just in case the originals move somewhere.
The document does not have the status of a law; it is a recommendation for interpreting existing EU consumer protection laws regarding computer games. As I understand it, each country decides separately whether to follow these recommendations or not.
I have mixed feelings towards such regulations.
On one hand, the nonsense that goes on in free-to-play games (especially mobile ones) should have been stopped a long time ago. From my ethical position, I fully support attempts to bring order there.
On the other hand, regulations always complicate life for small and medium businesses and have little effect on large companies. The larger the company, the easier it is for it to ignore regulations.
In the following text, I'll list the main theses of the document, speculate on how these recommendations should be implemented according to the authors' intent, and how they will most likely be implemented in reality.
Also, the document is small — only 8 pages — and nicely formatted, so you can read it yourself.
Disclaimer
I'm not a lawyer and have nothing to do with free-to-play for about 5 years, so don't take my thoughts as recommendations.
Think of this text as an interesting exercise, a free flight of thought.
Theses
Simplified, in my own words.
In-game currency is recognized as a digital representation of real-world money if the primary purpose of this currency is to purchase something in the game.
In-game transactions are equivalent to real-world transactions in terms of consumer rights protection.
It is prohibited to use practices that exploit cognitive biases to make the player pay more or receive less.
The price in real-world currency must always be displayed next to the price in in-game currency.
It is recommended not to introduce multiple currencies and complicated exchange chains.
It is recommended not to force players to buy more currency than they need. For example, do not sell currency in fixed bundles, especially those that do not match the prices in the game (packs of 1000 coins when the cost of the desired item is 1001 coins).
All currency spending proposals must be accompanied by detailed transaction information, including a clear description of the purchased items and (maybe) a link to the description of consumer rights.
The player has the right to cancel the transaction within 14 days unless they've explicitly waived this right.
The player has the right to cancel the transaction if they believe they received a product that does not match the description. For example, if they received a sword with a different sprite or that sword didn't help them kill the boss they expected to kill.
In particular, partial rollback of transactions is recommended — refunding real-world money for the remaining unspent in-game currency.
Game operators should not confuse players with overcomplicated terms, delete something from the game (especially if it's purchasable), modify the costs of in-game currency, permanently ban players without the possibility of contesting the ban.
Game operators should especially carefully handle vulnerable clients. Of course, children, but there are more interesting options. For example, a person outside the game may not be considered vulnerable, still, in the game, they may start to be considered vulnerable if the game targets specific vulnerabilities such as gambling addiction, shopping addiction, etc.
"Whales" can be considered vulnerable clients, as their behavior suggests issues with impulse control and gambling. Therefore, all games targeting "whales" are likely considered to be targeting vulnerable clients.
Parental control functions should be implemented in the game. It is possible to use platform-provided functions.
It looks like a lot of fun :-)
How difficult it is to follow the regulations
For the start, let's
assess the complexity of following the letter and spirit of the recommendations
. What might be required of bona fide developers of free-to-play games?
Obviously, following the recommendations to the letter and spirit is expensive and complicated. I won’t try to prove that here; instead, I'll focus on what exactly makes it difficult and expensive.
Market restrictions
The first thing to decide is whether you are making the game only for the European Union or the whole world. This affects, at least, a number of interface and balance variants you should create.
The EU's free-to-play market, at its best, is the third largest after the USA and China.
Therefore, if you want a lot of free-to-play money, it is currently more profitable to ignore Europe by simply not releasing the game there. When and if you have a big bag of money, you may consider adapting the gam

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: PyReason是一个可解释的推理软件，支持基于图结构的注释、实值和时态逻辑推理。它使用逻辑规则和初始条件进行推理，适用于神经符号人工智能领域。该工具可以作为Python库通过pip安装，支持Python 3.7至3.10版本，其中多核并行支持需要Python 3.9或以上版本。软件遵循BSD-2-Clause许可证，相关商标归亚利桑那州立大学所有。更多文档和示例可在其ReadTheDocs页面查看。如使用该软件，需引用其2023年AAAI会议论文。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个软件库的实用性、易用性以及技术问题进行了讨论，尤其关注非学术用户如何理解该库，以及在使用过程中遇到的技术故障。

不同观点：
• Tokumei-no-hito认为该库的介绍对于非学术界的用户不够友好，希望有人能提供一个通俗易懂的介绍，帮助外行人理解该库的功能和用途。
• m1sta__对该库的实用性提出质疑，指出其在使用过程中遇到的几个问题。具体而言，他提到基本示例无法正常运行（出现递归深度超出错误），并且对API设计中规则以字符串形式传递的做法表示不满。

补充讨论：
• m1sta__提供了具体的错误示例，展示了他在Google Colab环境中运行代码时遇到的错误信息（"RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded"），这表明库在处理某些操作时可能存在技术问题或限制。
• 争议的焦点在于该库的易用性和稳定性。一方面，Tokumei-no-hito希望有更清晰的入门介绍，而m1sta__则直接指出了技术实现中的问题，特别是API设计和运行时错误。
• m1sta__的反馈还暗示了库的开发质量问题，特别是对于初学者或非学术用户来说，如果基本的示例代码无法顺利运行，可能会影响使用体验和信心。

总结：讨论围绕库的易用性和技术问题展开，Tokumei-no-hito关注非学术用户的理解问题，而m1sta__则指出了具体的技术故障和API设计上的不足。

3.10

3.9
and

data.title: Our Best Customers Are Now Robots
data.author: kiwicopple

本文由Fly.io的Kurt Mackey撰写，讨论了平台开发者体验（DX）和机器人自动化对其业务的影响。Fly.io一直以提供优秀的开发者体验为核心，特别是其命令行工具（CLI），如`flyctl launch`，能让用户快速部署应用。然而，最近平台的增长主要来自“机器人”用户，而非人类。

现代机器人由大量矩阵和简单方程构成，主要需求是向量运算和生成代码（称为“vibe coding”）。这些机器人用户需要快速启动和停止虚拟机（Fly Machines），以进行短期任务，如测试代码或运行服务器。Fly.io的平台特性，如快速启动和按需计费，特别适合这些需求。

有趣的是，机器人使用增量方式构建虚拟机，这与传统开发实践不同，但对机器人非常高效。作者承认，这种趋势使得以往对人类用户的解释变得无效，但机器人却从中获得很大价值。

主要讨论点：UX/DX（用户体验/开发者体验）与LLMs（大型语言模型）的关系，以及在云平台上如何处理LLMs的权限和安全性问题。

不同观点：
• [cadamsdotcom] 认为优秀的UX/DX设计不仅对人类用户有益，也对LLMs有很大帮助。他强调了良好的文档、反馈机制、可预测性、结构化、成熟度以及易于回溯等特点对LLMs的重要性。他还指出，提升UX/DX有助于将来对代理行为的审计，并建议fly.io继续专注于UX/DX，因为这对RX（机器人体验）也有很大影响。

• [adenta] 关注的是在现代云平台上如何处理LLMs的权限问题。他建议通过令牌化OAuth令牌来实现访问隔离，这样LLMs只能获得一个占位令牌，而由硬件隔离的机器来替换为真实的令牌。他还提出下一步应该是防止Fly平台本身访问这些令牌，以增强安全性。

• [skeptrune] 对将LLMs称为"机器人"提出异议，认为这可能引起混淆，建议使用"AI"或"Agent"这样的术语更为恰当。他还总结了原帖的观点，认为LLMs的兴起增加了对远程开发环境的需求，使得这方面的业务前景看好。

补充讨论：
• [bitwize] 以讽刺的口吻评论fly.io通过吸引GPT相关开发者来增强其平台吸引力，暗示平台可能在迎合当前的LLMs潮流。

争议焦点：
• 是否应该将LLMs称为"机器人"。[skeptrune] 认为这种称呼不准确且容易引起混淆，建议使用"AI"或"Agent"。
• 如何在云平台上安全地处理LLMs的权限问题。[adenta] 提出了令牌化OAuth令牌的解决方案，并进一步讨论了如何防止平台本身访问这些令牌以增强安全性。

Kurt Mackey

Annie Ruygt
Weâre Fly.io, a developer-focused public cloud. We turn Docker containers into hardware-isolated virtual machines running on our own metal around the world. We spent years coming up with
a developer experience we were proud of
. But now the robots are taking over, and they donât care.
It’s weird to say this out loud!
For years, one of our calling cards was “developer experience”. We made a decision, early on, to be a CLI-first company, and put a lot effort into making that CLI seamless. For a good chunk of our users, it really is the case that you can just
flyctl launch
from a git checkout and have an app containerized and deployed on the Internet. We haven’t always nailed these details, but we’ve really sweated them.
But a funny thing has happened over the last 6 months or so. If you look at the numbers, DX might not matter that much. That’s because the users driving the most growth on the platform aren’t people at all. They'reâ¦ robots.
What The Fuck Is Happening?
Here’s how we understand what we’re seeing. You start by asking, “what do the robots want?”
Yesterday’s robots had diverse interests. Alcohol. The occasional fiddle contest. A purpose greater than passing butter. The elimination of all life on Earth and the harvesting of its cellular iron for the construction of 800 trillion paperclips. No one cloud platform could serve them all.
[*] We didnât make up this term. Donât blame us.
Today’s robots are different. No longer masses of wire, plates, and transistors, modern robots are comprised of
thousands of stacked matrices knit together with some simple equations
. All these robots want are vectors. Vectors, and a place to burp out more vectors. When those vectors can be interpreted as source code, we call this process “vibe coding”[*].
We seem to be coated in some kind of vibe coder attractant. I want to talk about what that might be.
If you want smart people to read a long post, just about the worst thing you can do is to sound self-promotional. But a lot of this is going to read like a brochure. The problem is, Iâm not smart enough to write about the things weâre seeing without talking our book. I tried, and ended up tediously hedging every other sentence. Weâre just going to have to find a way to get through this together.
You Want Robots? Because This Is How You Get Robots
Compute.
The basic unit of computation on Fly.io is the
Fly Machine
, which is a Docker container running as a hardware virtual machine.
Not coincidentally, our underlying hypervisor engine is the same as Lambdaâs.
There’s two useful points of reference to compare a Fly Machine to, which illustrate why we gave them this pretentious name. The first and most obvious is an AWS EC2 VM. The other is an AWS Lambda invocation. Like a Lambda invocation, a Fly Machine can start like it’s spring-loaded, in double-digit millis. But unlike Lambda, it can stick around as long as you want it to: you can run a server, or a 36-hour batch job, just as easily in a Fly Machine as in an EC2 VM.
A vibe coding session generates code conversationally, which is to say that the robots stir up frenzy of activity for a minute or so, but then chill out for minutes, hours, or days. You can create a Fly Machine, do a bunch of stuff with it, and then stop it for 6 hours, during which time we’re not billing you. Then, at whatever random time you decide, you can start it back up again, quickly enough that you can do it in response to an HTTP request.
Just as importantly, the companies offering these vibe-coding services have lots of paying users. Meaning, they need a lot of VMs; VMs that come and go. One chat session might generate a test case for some library and be done inside of 5 minutes. Another might generate a Node.js app that needs to stay up long enough to show off at a meeting the next day. It’s annoying to do this if you can’t turn things on and off quickly and cheaply.
The core of this is a feature of the platform that we have
never been able to explain effectively to humans
. There are two ways to start a Fly Machine: by
creating
it with a Docker container, or by
starting
it after it’s already been
created
, and later
stopped
.
Start
is lightning fast; substantially faster than booting up even a non-virtualized K8s Pod. This is too subtle a distinction for humans, who (reasonably!) just mash the
create
button to boot apps up in Fly Machines. But the robots are getting a lot of value out of it.
Storage.
Another weird thing that robot workflows do is to build Fly Machines up incrementally. This feels really wrong to us. Until we discovered our robot infestation, we’d have told you not to do to this. Ope!
A typical vibe coding session boots up a Fly Machine out of some minimal base image, and then, once running, adds packages, edits source code, and adds
systemd
units  (robots understand
systemd
; it’s how they’re going to replace us). This is antithetical to normal contain

data.title: Trump seeks to end climate research at premier U.S. climate agency
data.author: pmags
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对通过停止检测或否认科学事实来影响数据或现实的做法的批评与历史类比

不同观点：
• 第一个评论（outer_web）提到了一种讽刺性的观点，即通过停止测试来让疫情数字下降，暗示这种做法是荒谬的，因为问题并没有真正解决，只是数据上看不到了。这个评论隐含了对通过掩盖或忽视问题来操控结果的批评。

• 第二个评论（pornel）通过历史类比进一步扩展了这一观点，提到了苏联在斯大林时期因为政治原因而禁止基因学研究的事件（李森科事件）。这个评论指出，历史上曾有因为政治或意识形态原因而扭曲科学的例子，导致了严重的后果。这是对通过政治干预科学可能带来的危害的警示。

• 第三个评论（hyperhello）简洁地表达了对上述历史事件的震惊和不可理解，强调这种做法是疯狂的。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了“停止测试以降低疫情数字”和“苏联李森科事件”两个例子，虽然背景不同，但都指向了通过否认或扭曲科学事实来影响现实的问题。
• 争议的焦点在于科学与政治的关系，以及当政治干预科学时可能带来的负面影响。这一问题在不同历史和社会背景下都有出现，显示了其复杂性和普遍性。
• 评论中的语气多为批评和震惊，表明了对通过操控科学或数据来影响现实的做法的普遍反对。

data.title: Palantir Is Helping Doge with a Massive IRS Data Project
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: Palantir与Elon Musk的“政府效率部门”（DOGE）合作，参与为国税局（IRS）构建一个新的“大型API”项目，旨在创建一个统一的API层，用于访问所有IRS数据库。该项目在一次“黑客松”活动中进行，数十名IRS工程师与Palantir代表合作，计划在30天内完成。该API将允许访问纳税人信息，包括姓名、地址、社会安全号码、报税表和就业数据，并可能将数据迁移至云端。DOGE希望Palantir的Foundry软件成为IRS系统的“数据中心”，使用户能够查看甚至修改数据。Foundry平台可组织数据、构建应用程序并运行AI模型，从而快速查询和处理敏感信息。该项目由前SpaceX工程师、健康科技公司CEO Sam Corcos领导，旨在提升IRS系统效率，并已削减15亿美元现代化预算。这一举措与特朗普总统的一项行政命令一致，旨在消除“信息孤岛”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Palantir及相关事件的看法，涉及政府行为、数据隐私、企业影响力等方面。

不同观点：
• JumpCrisscross认为，初步的报道不错，但需要进一步记录相关人员，特别是决策层以及执行层的个人信息，以便未来通过法律手段追究责任或采取其他行动。
• WarOnPrivacy批评将美国敏感数据提供给Palantir的行为，认为此举将对美国人民造成前所未有的剥削，且其负面影响将持续几代人。
• blendo对活动组织表示不满，认为会议缺乏结构性，像是一场噩梦般的撤退，尽管可能有一些优秀的开发者参与，但整体显得混乱，唯一的好处可能是拿到了一些不错的T恤。
• kowabungalow质疑政府的过度干预，并怀疑一个以获取经济利益为目标的组织能否真正提供公正的监督，暗示政府和企业都有可能滥用权力。
• ilrwbwrkhv则对Palantir获得合同的原因表示怀疑，质疑这是否与Musk、J.D. Vance和Trump的密切关系有关，还是因为他们确实是最佳选择。

补充讨论：
• atombender提供了一个存档链接，可能与讨论相关的背景资料或进一步的信息有关。
• 争议焦点之一是Palantir获得合同的合法性和正当性，以及其与政府高层的关系是否影响了合同的授予。
• 另一个争议点是政府和企业合作对公众隐私和权利的潜在威胁，以及如何对这些权力进行有效监督。

总体而言，评论反映了公众对数据隐私、政府行为和企业影响力的广泛关注，以及对透明度和问责制的需求。

Palantir, the software company cofounded by Peter Thiel, is part of an effort by Elon Musk’s so-called Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) to build a new “mega API” for accessing Internal Revenue Service records, IRS sources tell WIRED.
For the past three days, DOGE and a handful of Palantir representatives, along with dozens of career IRS engineers, have been collaborating to build a single API layer above all IRS databases at an event previously characterized to WIRED as a “
hackathon
,” sources tell WIRED. Palantir representatives have been onsite at the event this week, a source with direct knowledge tells WIRED.
APIs are application programming interfaces, which enable different applications to exchange data and could be used to move IRS data to the cloud and access it there. DOGE has expressed an interest in the API project possibly touching all IRS data, which includes taxpayer names, addresses, social security numbers, tax returns, and employment data. The IRS API layer could also allow someone to compare IRS data against interoperable datasets from other agencies.
Should this project move forward to completion, DOGE wants Palantir’s Foundry software to become the “read center of all IRS systems,” a source with direct knowledge tells WIRED, meaning anyone with access could view and have the ability to possibly alter all IRS data in one place. It’s not currently clear who would have access to this system.
Foundry is a Palantir platform that can organize, build apps, or run AI models on the underlying data. Once the data is organized and structured, Foundry’s “ontology” layer can generate APIs for faster connections and machine learning models. This would allow users to quickly query the software using artificial intelligence to sort through agency data, which would require the AI system to have access to this sensitive information.
Engineers tasked with finishing the API project are confident they can complete it in 30 days, a source with direct knowledge tells WIRED.
Got a Tip?
Are you a current or former government employee who wants to talk about what's happening? We'd like to hear from you. Using a nonwork phone or computer, contact the reporter securely on Signal at makenakelly.32.
Palantir has made
billions
in government contracts. The company develops and maintains a variety of software tools for enterprise businesses and government, including Foundry and Gotham, a data-analytics tool primarily used in defense and intelligence. Palantir CEO Alex Karp recently referenced the “disruption” of DOGE’s cost-cutting initiatives and said, “Whatever is good for America will be good for Americans and very good for Palantir.” Former Palantir workers have also taken over key
government IT
and
DOGE roles
in recent months.
WIRED was the first to report that
the IRS’s DOGE team was staging a “hackathon”
in Washington, DC, this week to kick off the API project. The event started Tuesday morning and ended Thursday afternoon. A source in the room this week explained that the event was “very unstructured.” On Tuesday, engineers wandered around the room discussing how to accomplish DOGE’s goal.
The Treasury Department did not respond to a request for comment confirming Palantir’s role in the project.
“The Treasury Department is pleased to have gathered a team of long-time IRS engineers who have been identified as the most talented technical personnel. Through this coalition, they will streamline IRS systems to create the most efficient service for the American taxpayer," a Treasury spokesperson tells WIRED. "This week, the team participated in the IRS Roadmapping Kickoff, a seminar of various strategy sessions, as they work diligently to create efficient systems. This new leadership and direction will maximize their capabilities and serve as the tech-enabled force multiplier that the IRS has needed for decades.”
The project is being led by Sam Corcos, a health-tech CEO and a former SpaceX engineer, with the goal of making IRS systems more “efficient,” IRS sources say. In meetings with IRS employees over the past few weeks, Corcos has discussed pausing all engineering work and canceling current contracts to modernize the agency’s computer systems, sources with direct knowledge tell WIRED. Corcos has also spoken about some aspects of these cuts publicly: “We've so far stopped work and cut about $1.5 billion from the modernization budget. Mostly projects that were going to continue to put us down the death spiral of complexity in our code base,” Corcos told Laura Ingraham on
Fox News in March
. Corcos is also a
special adviser
to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
Palantir and Corcos did not immediately respond to requests for comment

• blendo对活动组织表示不满，认为会议缺乏结构性，像是一场噩梦般的撤退，尽管可能有一些优秀的开发者参与，但整体显得混乱，唯一的好处可能是拿到了一些不错的T恤。
• kowabungalow质疑政府的过度干预，并怀疑一个以获取经济利益为目标的组织能否真正提供公正的监督，暗示政府和企业都有可能滥用权力。
• ilrwbwrkhv则对Palantir获得合同的原因表示怀疑，质疑这是否与Musk、J.D. Vance和Trump的密切关系有关，还是因为他们确实是最佳选择。

• atombender提供了一个存档链接，可能与讨论相关的背景资料或进一步的信息有关。
• 争议焦点之一是Palantir获得合同的合法性和正当性，以及其与政府高层的关系是否影响了合同的授予。
• 另一个争议点是政府和企业合作对公众隐私和权利的潜在威胁，以及如何对这些权力进行有效监督。

data.article_summary: 2025年，新墨西哥州成为美国首个为大多数家庭提供免费托儿服务的州，帮助约12万人脱贫。该州长期在儿童福利方面排名垫底，托儿费用高昂，曾给许多家庭带来沉重负担。例如，Lisset Sanchez曾因托儿费用几乎辍学，但免费托儿让她顺利完成学业并进入护理学校。同时，托儿工作者如Ofelia Gonzalez也受益于更高的工资，生活得到改善。新墨西哥州通过扩大疫情期间的援助政策，为家庭收入在联邦贫困线400%以下的家庭提供免费托儿，显著缓解了贫困问题。同时，该州增加对托儿工作者的工资，使托儿行业中的贫困率从27.4%降至16%。经济学家James Heckman的研究显示，投资于高质量的早期儿童教育可带来显著的社会和经济回报。新墨西哥州正通过大规模投资早期教育，试图进一步改善儿童福利和家庭经济状况。

43660147.article_content:
Pre-K students do a drawing activity at Mis Conejitos in Albuquerque, New Mexico, on 27 March 2025.
Photograph: Isabel Miranda/The Guardian
View image in fullscreen
Pre-K students do a drawing activity at Mis Conejitos in Albuquerque, New Mexico, on 27 March 2025.
Photograph: Isabel Miranda/The Guardian
Unequal beginnings
New Mexico
New Mexico made childcare free. It lifted 120,000 people above the poverty line
The state, which has long ranked worst in the US for child wellbeing, became the first and only in the country to offer free childcare to a majority of families
Supported by
About this content
Cecilia Nowell
in Albuquerque
Fri 11 Apr 2025 10.00 EDT
Last modified on Fri 11 Apr 2025 10.09 EDT
Share
There was a moment, just before the pandemic, when Lisset Sanchez thought she might have to drop out of college because the cost of keeping her three children in daycare was just too much.
Even with support from the state, she and her husband were paying $800 a month – about half of what Sanchez and her husband paid for their mortgage in Las Cruces,
New Mexico
.
But during the pandemic, that cost went down to $0. And Sanchez was not only able to finish college, but enroll in nursing school. With a scholarship that covered her tuition and free childcare, Sanchez could afford to commute to school, buy groceries for her growing family – even after she had two more children – and pay down the family’s mortgage and car loan.
“We are a one-income household,” said Sanchez, whose husband works while she is in school. Having free childcare “did help tremendously”.
View image in fullscreen
Giovanni Aguilar, three, and pre-K students listening to a story read by Brenda Soria, pre-k teacher in Albuquerque on 27 March 2025.
Photograph: Isabel Miranda/The Guardian
Around the same time, Ofelia Gonzalez and her sister began receiving assistance from the state to develop their at-home childcare center in south-western Albuquerque, called Mis Conejitos. The state started reimbursing their work at higher rates, which allowed them to buy toys and swings for the backyard, and raised wages for childcare workers across the state, which allowed Gonzalez to begin saving “so that I can have good credit and in time I can have my own home”, she said in Spanish.
The changes in Sanchez and Gonzalez’s lives are intertwined. Three years ago, New Mexico became the first state in the nation
to offer free childcare
to a majority of families. The United States has no federal, universal childcare – and ranks 40th on
a Unicef ranking
of 41 high-income countries’ childcare policies, while maintaining some of
the highest childcare costs
in the world. Expanding on pandemic-era assistance, New Mexico made childcare free for families earning up to 400% of the federal poverty level, or about $124,000 for a family of four. That meant about half of New Mexican children now qualified.
In one of the poorest states in the nation, where
the median household income is half that
and childcare costs for two children could
take up 80% of a family’s income
, the impact was powerful. The state, which had long ranked worst in the nation for child wellbeing, saw its poverty rate begin to fall.
View image in fullscreen
Portrait of Ofelia Gonzalez, director at Mis Conejitos in Albuquerque.
Photograph: Isabel Miranda/The Guardian
As the state simultaneously raised wages for childcare workers, and became the
first
to base its subsidy reimbursement rates on the actual cost of providing such care, early childhood educators were also raised out of poverty. In 2020,
27.4%
of childcare providers – often women of color – were living in poverty. By 2024, that number had
fallen to 16%
.
During the state’s recent legislative session, lawmakers approved
a “historic” increase
in funding for education, including early childhood education, that might improve those numbers even further.
“This is a big investment that we know is going to pay off,” said Elizabeth Groginsky, cabinet secretary of New Mexico’s nascent early childhood education and care department. She points to
research
from the Nobel-winning economist James Heckman that “every dollar spent on high-quality, birth-to-five programs for disadvantaged children can deliver a 13% per annum return on investment from better education and health outcomes for children, employment gains for parents, greater economic productivity and reduced spending on healthcare and crime.
“The governor has seen that this investment in our human capital is as important as all the investments we’re making in our infrastructure,” said Groginsky.
Despite the fact that widespread poverty has kept the state’s child wellbeing rates low, “New Mexico had, almost from statehood, a real culture around caring for children,” said Hailey Heinz, a senior research scientist and deputy director of the University of New Mexico’s Cradle to Career Policy Institute.
View image in fullscreen
Pre-K students doing movement exercises at Mis Conejitos in Albuquerque.

data.title: Show HN: Omiword – A daily, sector-based word puzzle
data.author: DamnInteresting
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个拼字游戏的玩法和规则。玩家需要在不同区域内拖动字母块，拼出四个常见的单词。每个谜题可能有多种解决方案。游戏从周一到周日逐渐增加难度。玩家可以看到自己的胜利场次和独特的代码，并能通过反馈调整音量或访问谜题档案。游戏结束后会显示所用时间和移动步数。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：玩家对单词游戏的体验反馈与功能建议

不同观点：
• **正面评价**：
  - james_david、psolidgold、bergie3000、totallykvothe、0xEF等玩家对游戏的整体设计、菜单UI和声音效果表示赞赏，认为游戏有趣且具有挑战性。
  - bergie3000和0xEF特别提到声音设计巧妙，暂时没有关闭音乐的意愿。
  - totallykvothe提到声音效果让他微笑，并期待更多谜题。

• **关于声音与视觉效果的争议**：
  - hasbot、psolidgold、fuzzer371、BaudouinVH等玩家认为声音和光效（拖动字母时的声光效果）可能会干扰游戏体验，建议添加静音选项或移除这些效果，以便玩家能更专注于解谜。
  - BaudouinVH质疑光效和声音是否有意增加游戏难度，认为这可能不符合玩家的实际需求。

• **关于难度与提示功能的讨论**：
  - smallerfish、fuzzer371、notarealllama等玩家认为游戏难度较高，建议加入提示功能（如显示部分答案或交换字母位置）以降低难度。
  - fuzzer371建议增加“揭示提示”按钮，允许玩家在需要时获得提示，同时可能受到分数惩罚。
  - notarealllama直接建议加入“提示模式”，帮助玩家解谜。

• **关于UI和操作性的反馈**：
  - smallerfish建议字母不应掉落在网格边界外，且字母交换位置应更方便，以减少繁琐操作。
  - hasbot建议加入难度选择功能，允许玩家根据自己的水平选择不同难度的谜题。
  - totallykvothe提到拖动边缘时容易误触手机的返回手势，建议改进UI设计以避免此类问题。

• **关于单词合法性与字典问题的争议**：
  - mjlawson和quuxplusone指出游戏中存在不合法的单词（如“Asse”）和不合适的单词（如“PYRUS”、“YACK”），并建议调整字典。
  - quuxplusone提到需要区分“合法单词”和“目标单词”，避免生成有多个合法解决方案的谜题，并引用了HueWords的设计思路。

• **关于多语言支持的建议**：
  - 0xEF询问未来是否会考虑支持其他语言，显示了对游戏国际化的期待。

补充讨论：
- jwong_对游戏中字母变“直”的机制感到困惑，认为这种设计容易引起误解，尤其是在字母组合不构成实际单词的情况下。
- avandekleut分享了自己的解谜经验，认为游戏具有挑战性但并非不可能完成，表达了对游戏的喜爱。

争议焦点：
- 声音与光效是否应默认开启，或是否应允许玩家轻松关闭。
- 游戏字典中的单词合法性问题以及是否应允许有多个解决方案的谜题存在。

data.title: That groan you hear is users' reaction to Recall going back into Windows
data.author: cratermoon
data.article_summary: 微软重新推出了Recall功能，该功能将每三秒钟截屏并存储用户在Windows 11上的所有操作。尽管用户可选择加入并控制是否暂停该功能，但其仍引发了隐私和安全专家的强烈反对。批评者担心，这可能被恶意内部人员或犯罪分子利用，成为敏感信息的“金矿”，尤其在涉及隐私保护的通讯内容时。即便用户A未选择加入，其信息仍可能被使用Recall的其他人无意间存储。该功能的数据库易被法律或政府传唤，并可能成为黑客目标。微软的这一举动被视为对用户不利的“劣化”行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows 11 新功能 "Recall" 及其隐私、安全、性能影响

不同观点：
• [Henchman21] 认为Windows 10的广告已经让人难以忍受，而Windows 11的新功能可能成为压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草，建议转向Linux桌面系统。
• [asperous] 指出该功能可能是选择性加入的，可能对某些人有用，比如帮助找到文件，但对注重隐私和安全的用户来说代价太大，并担心未来可能变为默认开启。

Security and privacy advocates are girding themselves for another uphill battle against Recall, the AI tool rolling out in Windows 11 that will screenshot, index, and store everything a user does every three seconds.
When Recall was first introduced in May 2024, security practitioners roundly castigated it for creating a gold mine for malicious insiders, criminals, or nation-state spies if they managed to gain even brief administrative access to a Windows device. Privacy advocates warned that Recall was ripe for abuse in intimate partner violence settings. They also noted that there was nothing stopping Recall from preserving sensitive disappearing content sent through privacy-protecting messengers such as Signal.
Enshittification at a new scale
Following months of backlash, Microsoft later suspended Recall. On Thursday, the company
said
it was reintroducing Recall. It currently is available only to insiders with access to the Windows 11 Build 26100.3902 preview version. Over time, the feature will be rolled out more broadly. Microsoft officials wrote:
Recall (preview)* saves you time by offering an entirely new way to search for things you’ve seen or done on your PC securely. With the AI capabilities of Copilot+ PCs, it’s now possible to quickly find and get back to any app, website, image, or document just by describing its content. To use Recall, you will need to opt-in to saving snapshots, which are images of your activity, and enroll in Windows Hello to confirm your presence so only you can access your snapshots. You are always in control of what snapshots are saved and can pause saving snapshots at any time. As you use your Copilot+ PC throughout the day working on documents or presentations, taking video calls, and context switching across activities, Recall will take regular snapshots and help you find things faster and easier. When you need to find or get back to something you’ve done previously, open Recall and authenticate with Windows Hello. When you’ve found what you were looking for, you can reopen the application, website, or document, or use Click to Do to act on any image or text in the snapshot you found.
Microsoft is hoping that the concessions requiring opt-in and the ability to pause Recall will help quell the collective revolt that broke out last year. It likely won’t for various reasons.
First, even if User A never opts in to Recall, they have no control over the setting on the machines of Users B through Z. That means anything User A sends them will be screenshotted, processed with optical character recognition and Copilot AI, and then stored in an indexed database on the other users’ devices. That would indiscriminately hoover up all kinds of User A's sensitive material, including photos, passwords, medical conditions, and encrypted videos and messages. As
Privacy Guides
writer Em
wrote on Mastodon
:
This feature will unfortunately extract your information from whatever secure software you might have used and store it on this person's computer in a possibly less secure way.
Of course this person could manually take a screenshot of all of this anyway, but this feature makes it that even a well-intentioned person might either not be aware it is on, or might wrongly assume it is secure enough.
This feature isn't fully released yet, but it might be soon.
The presence of an easily searchable database capturing a machine’s every waking moment would also be a bonanza for others who don’t have users’ best interests at heart. That level of detailed archival material will undoubtedly be subject to subpoena by lawyers and governments. Threat actors who manage to get their spyware installed on a device will no longer have to scour it for the most sensitive data stored there. Instead they will mine Recall just as they do browser databases storing passwords now.
Microsoft didn’t immediately respond to a message asking why it’s reintroducing Recall less than a year after the feature got such a chilly reception. For critics, Recall is likely to remain one of the most pernicious examples of
enshittification
, the recently minted term for the shoehorning of unwanted AI and other features into existing products when there is negligible benefit to users.
Dan Goodin
Senior Security Editor
Dan Goodin
Senior Security Editor
Dan Goodin is Senior Security Editor at Ars Technica, where he oversees coverage of malware, computer espionage, botnets, hardware hacking, encryption, and passwords. In his spare time, he enjoys gardening, cooking, and following the independent music scene. Dan is based in San Francisco. Follow him at
here
on Mastodon and
here
on Bluesky. Contact him on Signal at DanArs.82.

data.title: Procedural Generation of Mammals and Locomotion
data.author: c6p
data.article_summary:
《The Big Forest》游戏中，作者希望创造既程序化生成又动态的生物，以适应森林地形。自2021年开始 sporadic 工作，2024年集中研究，前三个月专注于程序化模型生成，后三个月研究程序化动画。目标是生成逼真的森林生物，特别是像狐狸、熊等四足哺乳动物，这些生物需要具备合理的解剖结构和自然的运动方式。

作者从基本比例入手，通过低级参数生成生物模型，最终缩减为503个参数控制骨骼长度、旋转和皮肤距离等。为简化参数设置，作者开发了一种工具从蒙皮网格中提取数据，但因参考模型的蒙皮不一致，工具存在错误。2024年，作者已生成七种生物，但因模型格式问题丢失了部分原始模型。

简言之，作者正逐步克服技术难题，尝试通过程序化方式生成符合森林环境的3D生物模型和动画。

43641958.article_content:
For my game
The Big Forest
I want to have creatures that are both procedurally generated and animated, which, as expected, is quite a research challenge.
As mentioned in my
2024 retrospective
, I spent the last six months of 2024 working on this — three months on procedural model generation and three months on procedural animation. My work on the creatures actually started earlier though. According to my commit history, I started in 2021 after shipping
Eye of the Temple
for PCVR, though my work on it prior to 2024 was sporadic.
Though the creatures are still very far from where they need to be, I'll write a bit here about my progress so far.
The goal
I need lots of forest creatures for the gameplay of
The Big Forest
, some of which will revolve around identifying specific creatures to use for various unique purposes. I
prototyped the gameplay
using simple sprites for creatures, but the final game requires creatures that are fully 3D and fit well within the game's
forest terrain
.
I've seen a fair amount of projects with procedural creatures. It's not too hard to create a simple torso with legs, randomizing the configuration, and animating movement by transitioning the feet between footsteps in straight lines or simple arcs.
This works fine for bugs, spiders, lizards and other crawly critters, as well as for aliens and alien-like fantasy creatures. The project Critter Crosser is doing
very cool things with this
. While it features mammals too, I'm not sure they'd translate well outside the game's intentionally low-res, quirky aesthetic.
If we also consider games where only the animation is procedural,
Rain World
is another example where this works great for its low-definition but highly dynamic alien-like creatures.
Spore
is a classic example too, though its creatures often end up looking both alien and goofy.
For
The Big Forest
though, I want creatures that feel like they truly belong in a forest, with movement and design reminiscent of quadruped mammals like foxes, bears, lynx, squirrels, and deer. The way mammals look and move is far too distinct to simply "wing it" — at least in my game's aesthetic. Achieving realistic mammalian creatures requires thorough study, so although I also plan to include non-mammal creatures, I’m focusing primarily on mammals for now.
Procedural generation of creatures
The basic problem is to generate forest creatures with plausible anatomy with a small set of parameters and ensure that:
The parameters are
meaningful
so I can use them to get the results I want.
Any random values for the parameters will always create valid creatures.
My main challenge is identifying what constitutes meaningful parameters. This is something I have to discover gradually, starting with a large number of low-level parameters based on minimal assumptions and eventually narrowing down to a smaller set of high-level parameters as I refine the logic.
From the beginning, I decided to focus on basic proportions for the foreseeable future, without worrying about more subtle shape details. For this reason I limited the generated meshes to extruded rectangles. I had to start somewhere, and here's the glorious first mesh:
Later I specified the torso, each leg, each foot, the neck, head, jaw, tail, and each ear as multi-segmented extruded rectangles. I found this approach easily sufficient for capturing the likeness of different animals. By the end of 2023, I had produced these three creatures and the ability to interpolate between them:
This was based on very granular parameters, essentially a list of bones with alignment and thickness data. Each bone length, rotation values, and skin distance from the bone in various directions was an input parameter, totaling 503 parameters.
Creating creatures from scratch using these parameters was impractical, so I developed a tool to extract data from skinned meshes. The tool identified which vertices belonged to which bones and derived the thickness values from that. However, it was error-prone, partly due to inconsistent skinning of the reference models. For example, in the cat model, one of the tail bones wasn’t used in the skinning, which confused my script. This is why part of the cat’s tail is missing in the image above.
I tried to implement workarounds for such edge cases, and various ways to manually guide the script towards better results for each creature, but each new reference 3D model seemed to come with new types of quirks to handle. After resuming work in 2024, I had these seven creatures, with their reference 3D models shown below them:
(I lost two of my original reference 3D models — the coyote and bull elk — because they were in Maya format. Since I don’t have Maya installed, when a project reimport was triggered, Unity couldn’t import the models, and they vanished. Since it's not standard practice to commit Unity’s imported data (the Library folder) to source control, I couldn’t recover them.)

data.title: Grappling with Infinity in Constraint Solvers
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在约束求解器中处理无穷大的问题，以作者创建的编程语言Sentient为例。许多约束满足问题涉及无穷多个解，例如寻找两个整数使其和为10，这有无穷多组解。Sentient程序可以通过指定整数位数来限制求解范围，但默认情况下整数范围有限（如8位，范围是-128到127）。为了寻找更大范围的解，需要重启程序，导致重复搜索已探索过的区域，效率低下。虽然可以通过添加约束来避免重复搜索，但这很繁琐且容易出错。理想情况下，Sentient应支持自动处理此类问题。当前，Sentient将问题编译为有限的布尔方程（SAT），无法直接处理无穷大，但未来可能通过引入新变量来更好地近似无穷整数。

43630223.article_content:
tuzz.tech
blog
← Previous
Next Article →
Grappling with infinity in constraint solvers
Published
November 17, 2019
by
Chris Patuzzo
In 2016, I created a programming language called
Sentient
. Since then, I’ve had time to reflect and
think about the language. This series is about that.
Many constraint-satisfaction problems deal with infinity in some shape or form.
Even rudimentary problems, like "Find two integers that sum to 10". Solutions include:
(4, 6)
(-7, 17)
(-1953856112,
1953856122)
That (d)escalated quickly!
In fact, there are infinitely many solutions and infinitely many pairs of
integers to test. Here’s a
Sentient
program to
solve this problem:
int
a, b
;
invariant
a + b ==
10
;
expose
a, b
;
▲
A Sentient program to find integers that sum to 10
This article is about Sentient, but many of the concepts apply to constraint solvers in general.
We can run this with the
--number 0
option
,
to continuously find solutions:
▲
Finding multiple solutions with Sentient
When Sentient returns
{}
, it has exhausted the search space and can’t find any
more solutions.
After a few seconds this
program
terminates
which seems
wrong
. Why should a problem that has infinitely many solutions
ever terminate? Shouldn’t it run forever?
I sometimes use ‘program’ and ‘problem’ synonymously. Programs are descriptions of problems.
The simple answer is that integers in Sentient aren’t really integers as far as
the mathematical definition is concerned. Their magnitude is limited by how
many bits represent them. By
default
this is
8 but can be specified, e.g.
int9
,
int32
int
ranges from -128 to 127.
In many cases this is fine. We can pick a number of bits that’s ‘big enough’
and not worry about it. But other times it’s not fine. We often want to start
small and work our way up to larger representations, but that means restarting
the program each time.
For some problems, solutions are extremely rare (or non-existent) and it could
take weeks or months for
Sentient
to find
one. In these cases, it makes sense to start with small representations and
progressively rule our search spaces of increasing size.
A negative result for a small space is better than no result for a larger one.
Unfortunately, when a program is restarted, we lose its progress. Regions that
were already explored are explored again. If we increase
int
to
int9
,
Sentient finds new solutions but it also finds all the same solutions again.
This is wasteful.
We could compensate by adding a constraint:
int9
a, b
;
invariant
a <
-128
|| a >
127
|| b <
-128
|| b >
127
;
# ...
▲
Eliminating the region we’ve already explored
But
this
becomes unwieldy, and for many
problems, isn’t easy to specify. It’s also a manual process and therefore
error-prone. Ideally, Sentient would offer first-class support for something
like this. I have some ideas about how that might work.
This specifies that
a
or
b
must lie outside the region already explored for
eight-bit integers.
In
some cases
, I’ve
written scripts
to generate Sentient programs with integers of increasing size.
Approximations
I’ve
found
a useful way to think about this
is in terms of
approximations
. An eight-bit integer is really an
approximation of the mathematical (infinite) version of an integer. Its domain
is finite but as long as we stay within bounds, it behaves in the same way.
I’m using ‘approximation’ in a
literal
sense and not according to some precise
mathematical definition.
Most of the time when we write computer programs we don’t have to think about
this because we deal with concretions. Variables are assigned concrete values
and, provided we stay within range without overflowing, everything checks out.
In our case, variables are
‘symbolic’
. We
don’t actually assign values to
int a, b
, we just tell Sentient they exist and
specify some constraints. Its job is to discover values for
a, b
, but it has
to work with something tangible. It can’t reason about infinity.
‘Symbolic’ is the term used by the
KLEE
project for
this concept.
Why
can’t
Sentient reason about infinity?
Great question!
Technically it could but currently, its implementation closely relates to the
mechanism it uses for solving. Programs are compiled to instances of
SAT
which, by
definition, are boolean equations that comprise finitely many variables and
clauses.
This
doesn’t
have to be the case, though.
Sentient could abstract over these equations and automatically introduce new
variables to represent larger integers.
I think of this as
better approximating
the infinite version of an integer.
Actually,
Sentient
does something similar to
this for the
--number
option
.
Sentient finds multiple solutions to problems by repeatedly solving the same
equation. It introduces a new clause each time to ban the solution it just
found.
Sentient doesn’t solve these equations itself. It delegates to SAT solvers,
such as
lingeling
.
Could we dynamically change the size of representations?
We could, but it’s not obvious how to do this. If a program declares mult

Awe
ALGOL W is a successor to Algol 60 closely based on A Contribution to the Development of ALGOL by Niklaus Wirth and C. A. R. Hoare. It includes dynamically allocated records, string handling, complex numbers and a standard I/O system.
Awe is a new compiler for the ALGOL W language. It is a complete implementation of the language described in the
ALGOL W Language Description, June 1972
. Awe should be able to compile code intended for the OS/360 ALGOL W compilers with little or no modification. For details read the
Awe manual
,
awe
(1) and
awe.mk
(7).
The main requirements for compiling Awe are a Unix-like operating system, GCC, Python3, OCaml and Boehm GC. For details read
INSTALL
and awe(1).
Thank You
Thank you to: Hendrick Boom, Tony Marsland, Carey Bloodworth, John Boutland and Nicolas Brouard for a great deal of expert advice, encouragement and testing; and the authors of the
Algol W Language Description
for creating such an unambiguous work.
By the Way

. Frank kept me sane, somehow.

data.title: Dev Tools Honeytrap: Why We Can't Stop Building Tools Nobody Buys
data.author: lunarcave
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开发工具（Dev Tools）在技术和商业中的挑战与机遇

不同观点：
• **关于行业普遍性的质疑**：[8f2ab37a-ed6c] 认为每个行业的人都觉得自己的领域最难，不仅仅是开发工具。他提到了其他领域如健康科技、在线约会和教育科技等，暗示开发工具的挑战并非独一无二。

• **云服务对开发工具销售的影响**：[wavemode] 指出，许多公司不愿意在技术栈中添加新技术，因此更愿意支付外部供应商来运行这些工具，尤其是通过云服务的方式。这种现象导致了云托管服务市场的巨大需求，即使是一些自托管非常简单的软件。

• **自然选择与市场竞争的类比**：[simpaticoder] 使用自然选择的类比来描述软件的发展，强调了“突变”和“选择压力”在软件演化中的作用。从外部看，变化似乎是随机的，而成功往往由社会成功和运气驱动。此外，还提到流行工具往往会更流行，以及语言多样性受学术课程和招聘实践影响的现象。

• **开发工具与晋升机会的冲突**：[8f2ab37a-ed6c] 进一步提出，开发工具可能阻碍工程师的晋升机会，因为它们解决的问题不会为工程师的简历增加亮点。在大公司中，开发工具可能与“简历驱动开发”相冲突，因此在某种程度上注定失败。它们只有在公司早期阶段才有机会成长。

• **解决实际问题的重要性**：[encoderer] 认为虽然有些观点过于 cynical（愤世嫉俗），但他通过自己的创业经验（如2014年创建Cronitor）说明，解决实际问题才是关键。他强调从客户需求出发，逆向工作到技术，而不是从技术出发寻找客户。他批评了一些人从LLM（大型语言模型）技术出发寻找客户的做法，认为这是一个陷阱。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：开发工具是否真的在与工程师的晋升需求相冲突，以及开发工具在市场中的实际价值。
• **成功因素**：从实际问题出发开发工具的成功策略与从技术出发寻找应用场景的潜在陷阱。
• **市场现象**：云服务托管的广泛需求与公司对技术栈复杂性的厌恶。

这些观点共同描绘了开发工具在技术和商业中的多重挑战和机遇，以及不同视角下的策略和争议。

data.title: A Guide to Bearer Tokens: JWT vs. Opaque Tokens
data.author: bubblehack3r
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JWT（JSON Web Token）与不透明令牌（Opaque Token）在安全性、撤销机制和可扩展性方面的比较

不同观点：
• motorest认为文章对JWT的描述不准确，具体关于JWT难以撤销和可能泄露敏感数据的问题。他们指出，JWT的撤销可以通过将JWT ID添加到已撤销列表来实现，虽然需要资源服务器定期刷新该列表，但这并不复杂。至于敏感数据泄露问题，motorest指出，只有当开发者有意在JWT中包含敏感数据时，才会出现这种情况，JWT本身并不强制包含敏感信息。

• 文章的观点似乎更倾向于认为JWT在撤销和安全性方面存在固有的缺陷，并暗示不透明令牌在安全性和撤销控制上更具优势，但代价是增加了额外的开销和降低了可扩展性。

补充讨论：
• motorest进一步指出，文章的总体质量较差，可能是因为其对JWT和不透明令牌的对比存在误导性信息。

• motorest认为任何可以通过不透明令牌进行的安全和撤销检查，同样也可以通过JWT实现，暗示两者在功能上并没有文章所说的那么大差距。

• 争议的焦点在于JWT的撤销机制和敏感数据泄露问题。文章强调了JWT的潜在风险，而motorest则反驳这些风险是可以通过适当的设计和实现来管理的。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是可扩展性与安全性的权衡，文章指出不透明令牌在安全性和撤销控制上更好，但会增加开销和降低可扩展性，而motorest似乎不认同这种说法，认为JWT同样可以实现这些功能而不增加过多开销。

data.title: Googler... ex-Googler
data.author: namukang
data.article_summary: 本文是Google前员工Adam Argyle的个人陈述，描述了他突然被Google解雇的经历和感受。他提到自己的职位在毫无预兆的情况下被取消，无法再访问工作相关的文档和代码，感到非常伤心、愤怒和背叛。尽管他正在参与多个重要项目，如Google IO活动和CSS工作组，这些工作都因解雇而被迫中止。他形容自己仿佛只是大公司中的一颗无关紧要的齿轮，并表达了对多年培养的人际关系和职业成就瞬间失去的痛苦。文章最后他提供了新的联系方式，并收到了许多同行的安慰和支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：员工在面对大公司（如Google）裁员时的感受以及公司与员工关系的性质

不同观点：
• ivraatiems认为，员工对公司的贡献往往得不到应有的认可和回报，即使对公司有重大贡献，员工仍然可能随时被裁，因此没有动力去付出超过最低限度的工作努力。
• musicale认同公司（尤其是大公司）对待员工像对待可替代的零件，关系是纯粹交易性的，公司要求忠诚只是因为有利可图，而非出于 reciprocity（互惠）。
• walterbell通过分享Google裁员的新闻链接，指出即使是像Google这样的大公司也会进行大规模裁员，暗示这种情况在大公司中是常见的。
• tuna74强调员工在公司中只是“一个 cog”，员工不应期望公司会真正重视他们，提醒大家要随时做好准备。
• commandersaki对Google员工表示一定程度的不满，认为他们因为高薪和声望而不应被过度同情，认为他们会很快找到新的机会。
• minraws分享了自己类似的经历，虽然遭遇突然裁员，但最终找到了更高薪的工作，并鼓励其他有类似经历的人不要放弃希望，可能会有更好的机会。
• greatgib强烈建议员工不应过度投入时间和精力到公司，因为公司并不会对员工忠诚，员工也应该随时准备跳槽以寻求更好的机会。
• ein0p以过来人身份建议，离开大公司可能是“伪装的祝福”，鼓励被裁员工尝试去小公司工作，那里可能更把人当人看。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了公司裁员决策的非人性化处理方式，员工往往感到困惑和不满（greatgib）。
• 有人质疑公司裁员是否真的符合公司的长期利益（musicale），并提到反垄断等外部因素可能对公司决策的影响（musicale）。
• 一些评论者如 zem 和 minraws 提到，即使被裁员，之前建立的职业关系和人脉仍然可能带来帮助，建议保持联系和沟通。
• 部分评论者如 uptownfunk 和 canucker2016 提到了 Google 员工身份的特殊性，以及“Xoogler”这一术语的使用。

争议焦点：
• 是否应对Google等大公司员工表示同情，commandersaki认为他们因高薪和高声望而不需太多同情，但 minraws 和 greatgib 等人则强调裁员带来的情感冲击，并认为裁员处理方式不人道。
• 公司裁员是否符合公司长期利益，musicale和ein0p对此持怀疑态度，而walterbell等人则认为这是公司常见的结构性调整。

43658089.article_content:
Table of contents
Goodbye Google, I guess
I can't believe the timing
(214) Comments
Last night, my role at Google was eliminated. I'm quite sick to my stomach, extremely sad, and even more angry.
argyle@google.com
is no more. Just like that.
There's not really anything about this that makes sense.
Goodbye Google, I guess
#
I'm told this comes as a shock to my managers and other Chrome team leaders. I'm told it's not based on merit. I'm told I could find another role.
But I was also immediately ripped away from my calendar, docs, code, and more. Anything nice anyone has to say is immediately met with reality, and reality says "don't let the door hit you on the way out."
I can't believe the timing
#
I was at a Chrome team offsite, quite literally having some of the most fun with Chrome folks I've had in a while; shoulder to shoulder with incredible engineers, planning ways to make web developers life's easier while raising the quality level of the web.
It's like none of these good moments ever happened.
Like I was never in any of these room's or calls. Like I wasn't assigned to high priority features or an owner of meaningful work streams.
I was supposed to record a Google IO video next week. A talk I was
very
very excited to give. Gone. Wasted.
I was supposed to be on stage at Google IO, gone.
I was supposed to run a booth right outside the main stage, gone.
I was supposed to help with the developer keynote, ensuring things matched reality and were beautiful. Gone.
CSS Working Group membership, gone.
Developer Office Hours, gone.
Code access to the
Carousel Gallery
, gone.
Helping with Overflow 5, or other CSS work at Google, gone.
Relationships that took me years to cultivate… mostly going to be gone too.
The list of things I was doing is huge. It's going to be a while until I can resume some of them, and many of them won't resume at all.
I feel back stabbed, unappreciated, tossed in the trash. I can't sleep. I'm ashamed. I'm pissed.
I really was just a fuckin cog in a mega corp.
Find me on
Bluesky
or email me at
adam.is@nerdy.dev
if you feel compelled to reach out.
Sorry if I don't reply quickly, it's very overwhelming to read messages about this. The topic is quite sore.

) (the steak sauce) while speaking at the ASU+GSV education summit, an event put on by Silicon Valley investors. She was discussing modern classroom tools when she started to confuse the two terms.

“a school system that’s going to start making sure that first graders, or even pre-Ks, have A1 teaching in every year,” which she said was a “wonderful thing.”

But the comment wasn’t just an isolated slip of the tongue. McMahon added, “Kids are sponges. They just absorb everything. It wasn’t all that long ago that it was, ‘We’re going to have internet in our schools!’ Now let’s see A1 and how can that be helpful.”

The steak sauce company, a U.S. subsidiary of Kraft Heinz, then seemed to savor McMahon’s gaffe in particularly saucy posts to social media.
On X (formerly Twitter) and Instagram (

), accounts for A.1. Original Sauce wrote, “You heard her. Every school should have access to A.1.” alongside a bottle slapped with a logo that reads, “For education purposes only.” The graphic next to the bottle says, “Agree. Best to start them early.”

Confusingly, McMahon actually called artificial intelligence by its correct name (AI) earlier in the panel but became less consistent as she spoke.

McMahon, 76, was a controversial pick for education secretary given her lack of experience in the area; she was formerly the CEO of World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE), which she founded with her now-estranged husband, Vince. The Senate confirmed her position in the Trump cabinet in a 51-to-45 vote in early March.
Last month, Trump signed an executive order to begin dismantling the Department of Education to return the overseeing of education to the states and not the federal government.

data.title: DOJ Implements Security Program to Protect Sensitive Data from Adversaries
data.author: impish9208
data.article_summary:
2025年4月11日，美国司法部宣布实施一项关键的**数据安全计划**，以防止中国、俄罗斯、伊朗等外国对手通过商业活动获取和利用美国政府相关数据及美国公民的敏感个人数据，进行间谍活动、经济 espionage、监控和反情报行动，以及发展人工智能和军事能力，从而威胁美国国家安全。该计划依据**14117号行政命令**制定，包括出口管制措施，限制外国对手获取美国政府相关数据及基因组、地理位置、生物识别、健康、金融等敏感个人数据。

司法部国家安全司（NSD）发布了**合规指南**和**常见问题解答（FAQs）**，帮助公众遵循该计划，并在最初90天内实施有限的执法政策。指南提供了最佳实践和模型合同语言，FAQs则解答了有关行政命令和许可申请等问题。该计划于2025年4月8日生效，旨在应对紧迫的国家安全威胁。

Justice Department Implements Critical National Security Program to Protect Americans’ Sensitive Data from Foreign Adversaries
Friday, April 11, 2025
Share
Facebook
X
LinkedIn
Email
For Immediate Release
Office of Public Affairs
Department Answers Frequently Asked Questions, Provides Guidance, and Issues Limited Enforcement Policy for First 90 Days
Today, the Justice Department took significant steps to move forward with implementing a critical program to prevent China, Russia, Iran, and other foreign adversaries from using commercial activities to access and exploit U.S. government-related data and Americans’ sensitive personal data to commit espionage and economic espionage, conduct surveillance and counterintelligence activities, develop AI and military capabilities, and otherwise undermine our national security.
The Data Security Program implemented by the National Security Division (NSD) under
Executive Order 14117
addresses this “unusual and extraordinary threat…to the national security and foreign policy of the United States” that has been repeatedly recognized across political parties and by all three branches of government.
The Justice Department’s continued prioritization of the Data Security Program delivers on promises made by President Trump in his
America First Investment Policy
and
NSPM-2 on Imposing Maximum Pressure on Iran
, addresses threats identified in the
2025 Annual Threat Assessment of the U.S. Intelligence Community
and President Trump’s
2017 National Security Strategy
, and responds to the national emergency President Trump declared in
Executive Order 13873
.
“If you’re a foreign adversary, why would you go through the trouble of complicated cyber intrusions and theft to get Americans’ data when you can just buy it on the open market or force a company under your jurisdiction to give you access?” said Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche. “The Data Security Program makes getting that data a lot harder.”
To address this urgent threat, the
Data Security Program
establishes what are effectively export controls that prevent foreign adversaries, and those subject to their control, jurisdiction, ownership, and direction, from accessing U.S. government-related data and bulk genomic, geolocation, biometric, health, financial, and other sensitive personal data. To assist the public in coming into compliance with the Data Security Program, NSD has issued a
Compliance Guide
, an initial list of over 100
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
, and an
Implementation and Enforcement Policy
for the first 90 days. NSD will be taking additional steps over the coming weeks and months to implement the Data Security Program, including publishing an initial Covered Persons List that identifies and designates persons subject to the control and direction of foreign adversaries. The Data Security Program went into effect on April 8, 2025.
Newly Issued Guidance and FAQs
The Data Security Program Compliance Guide identifies and describes best practices for complying with the Data Security Program, thereby mitigating the unacceptable national security risk of enabling countries of concern to access and exploit Americans’ sensitive personal data. The document provides guidance on key definitions, prohibited and restricted transactions, and the requirements for building a robust data compliance program. The Compliance Guide also provides model contractual language and suggests best practices for complying with the Data Security Program’s audit and recordkeeping requirements. It is crucial that U.S. persons familiarize themselves and become prepared to comply with the Data Security Program’s prohibitions and restrictions once they became effective on April 8, 2025.
The Data Security Program FAQs address high-level clarifications about Executive Order 14117 and provides valuable information about the Data Security Program, its scope, and accompanying processes for requesting licenses and advisory opinions, making disclosures of Data Security Program violations, and reporting rejected prohibited transactions. The FAQs reflect some of the comprehensive feedback and common issues the Department received and addressed through the rulemaking process, both as public comments in response to the
Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking
and
Notice of Proposed Rulemaking
, as well as questions delivered during dozens of engagements with individuals, businesses, trade groups, and other stakeholders that were potentially interested in or impacted by the Data Security Program. NSD will update these FAQs as necessary and appropriate to address additional questions raised by the public.

43660078.article_summary:
2025年4月11日，美国司法部宣布实施一项关键的**数据安全计划**，以防止中国、俄罗斯、伊朗等外国对手通过商业活动获取和利用美国政府相关数据及美国公民的敏感个人数据，进行间谍活动、经济 espionage、监控和反情报行动，以及发展人工智能和军事能力，从而威胁美国国家安全。该计划依据**14117号行政命令**制定，包括出口管制措施，限制外国对手获取美国政府相关数据及基因组、地理位置、生物识别、健康、金融等敏感个人数据。

司法部国家安全司（NSD）发布了**合规指南**和**常见问题解答（FAQs）**，帮助公众遵循该计划，并在最初90天内实施有限的执法政策。指南提供了最佳实践和模型合同语言，FAQs则解答了有关行政命令和许可申请等问题。该计划于2025年4月8日生效，旨在应对紧迫的国家安全威胁。

data.title: Arroyo (YC W23) has been acquired by Cloudflare
data.author: necubi
data.article_summary: 2025年4月10日，Arroyo团队宣布加入Cloudflare。Arroyo已被Cloudflare收购，旨在将无服务器SQL流处理引入Cloudflare开发者平台，并与Queues、Workers和R2集成。Arroyo引擎将继续保持开源，并支持自托管。此次收购由Arroyo首席执行官Micah Wylde宣布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare的服务质量、客户支持与销售问题，以及其收购开源项目的声誉和战略

不同观点：
• [对Cloudflare服务和支持的批评] tiffanyh和prennert指出，Cloudflare的客户支持和销售服务非常差，即使是对付费用户也是如此。他们提到，即使尝试通过提交工单或拨打热线电话，也很难联系到销售人员。tiffanyh还提到，支持团队在用户刚成为客户时会优先处理问题，但一段时间后则难以获得回应。

• [对Cloudflare技术产品的认可] dm03514对Cloudflare收购Arroyo表示祝贺，并认为Arroyo有可能成为Flink和Spark Streaming的长期替代品。不过他们也提到Arroyo在配置上过于依赖UI，而不是API，因此在某些工作环境中难以推广。

• [对Cloudflare的讽刺与质疑] udev4096使用"Clownflare"一词讽刺Cloudflare，质疑其安全性及道德问题。esafak则质疑Cloudflare在维护开源项目方面的声誉。

• [对收购战略的比较] rebanevapustus质疑Arroyo相对于Materialize或Feldera的优势，认为Arroyo可能是这些产品的子集。

• [对开源项目收购的疑问] mentalgear对盈利公司收购开源项目的意图和可行性提出疑问，质疑这些项目是否真的可以被"购买"。

补充讨论：
• [对具体技术功能的期待] ambrood和moonikakiss对Iceberg catalog和R2的集成表示期待，并询问其优先级。

• [对个人成就的祝贺] 多个评论如jeffchao、brandonb和Hansenq仅对Micah及其团队的收购表示祝贺，未涉及具体技术或服务问题。

• [对收购价格的关注] ilrwbwrkhv直接询问收购的价格，显示出对交易细节的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare的客户支持和销售服务的质量是评论中的主要争议点，尤其是对于付费用户而言，这种服务体验令人不满。
• 另一个潜在的争议点是Cloudflare收购开源项目的声誉及这些项目未来的发展方向，部分用户对此持怀疑态度。

data.author: cmurf

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对特朗普和普京的比较及对他们性格和能力的评价

不同观点：
• 观点一：特朗普被视为“疯狂的邪恶”。该评论暗示特朗普虽然表现出疯狂的特质，但他缺乏像普京那样的智力和策略。这种观点将特朗普描述为一个不那么危险的人物，因为他缺乏像普京那样的支持者和理智。

• 观点二：普京被视为“冷算计的邪恶”。该评论认为普京是更为理智和有策略的领导者，拥有盟友和一定的智慧，这使他比特朗普更具威胁。这种观点强调了普京的冷静和计算能力，认为他是更为可怕的对手。

补充讨论：
• 评论中的对比显示了对两位领导人的负面评价，但侧重点不同。特朗普被描述为疯狂而无脑的邪恶，而普京则被视为冷静且有策略的邪恶。
• 争议的焦点可能在于对两位领导人的性格和能力的评价不同。一些人可能认为特朗普同样具备策略和智慧，而另一些人可能认为普京的疯狂不亚于特朗普。
• 评论还暗示了对全球政治领导人的一种不安和批评态度，特别是在涉及国际关系和领导能力时。
